To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the T cell memory responses directed towards HCMV develop and maintain over the lifetime of an individual and that there is only a limited evidence to support the concept of “memory inflation”.
the T cell response to HCMV in humans appears to be maintained over time and is directed against lytic and latent antigens.
the T cell memory responses in HCMV-infected individuals are not as robust as previously thought.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of T cell responses in humans to human cytomegalo virus (CMV).
the development and maintenance over time of immune responses directed towards HCMV in healthy people and in those with impaired immune systems.
how the human immune system responds to HCMV and how the immune response changes over the course of a lifetime.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HCMV T-cell memory response is maintained and functional over the course of life and is able to respond to both lytic and latent virus infection in a range of tissue sites.
the HCMV T-cell response to infection is maintained and is able to control HCMV replication in healthy people, but in the presence of immune dysfunction the virus can reactivate.
HCMV T cells do not undergo “memory inflation”, and that the immune response to HCMV is well controlled in healthy people.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HCMV T-cell response is maintained in the blood, but is not maintained in the tissues.
HCMV infection of humans results in the generation of a diverse repertoire of CD4 and CD8 T cells that is maintained over the life course.
there is a need for a better understanding of the T cell immune response to HCMV in humans, particularly during the latent phase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is still a lot to understand about the human immune response to HCMV and that further studies will be needed to understand how the immune system can best be manipulated to prevent disease.

the T cell memory responses directed towards HCMV are highly dynamic and are not simply a result of the virus being present in the body, but rather a result of a balance between the immune system and the virus.
there are still a large number of unanswered questions regarding how HCMV T cells respond to lytic and latency infection.
